peak_delay ≈ A + 8/17/26 ps: the small excess is the b√f dispersion (gd = A + b/4π√f > A at the pulse's low-frequency-weighted spectrum) — physically consistent. Energy loss (12–35%) is concentrated in the pulse's heavy right tail (its 3–10 GHz content sees 0.3–2 dB), while the core is nearly undistorted (peak 0.990/0.904/0.810 V vs input 1.078 V).

4) CONVENTIONS AS INSTRUCTED
- f=0 rows written with magnitude_db=0, phase_rad=0, attenuation=0, and group_delay = one-sided finite difference of the REPORTED phase array (5.4125/8.3682/11.4020 ns) — no NaNs. For f>0, gd = A + b/(4π√f) (exact derivative of the reported phase); verified: max |gd_reported − (−dφ/dω via np.gradient)| = 1.4–4.9e-11 s (only at 30 MHz, where the b√f curvature makes the central-difference approximation deviate from the exact derivative).
- phase_rad is the continuous unwrapped branch through 0 at f=0 (monotone decreasing; e.g. target_0 phase(62.5 GHz) = −2098.62 rad).
- Two-sided spectrum: H[0]=1 exactly; H[1..2047] = one-sided model values; conjugate mirror H_full[2049+k] = conj(H_full[2047−k]) for k=0..2046, i.e. H_full[k] = conj(H_full[N−k]) for all k, which guarantees a real output. NOTE: the literal formula in your note (H[2049+k]=conj(H[2048−k]), k=0..2047) is off-by-one for N=4049… I mean N=4096: it references the nonexistent index 4096 and would shift the mirror by one bin (making the output complex). I implemented the standard conjugate symmetry that realizes your intent; the Nyquist bin (2048) is forced real (model value there is complex, but |X| at 62.5 GHz ≈ 1e-30, so the change is ~1e-30).
- tail_asymmetry = (t_r−t_p)/(t_p−t_l) at the 50% level of the output pulse (documented in analysis.py docstring and inline comment); FWHM by linear interpolation; peak times by parabolic interpolation; energy_ratio = Σy²/Σx².

5) MINOR FINDINGS
- Corrected input FWHM = 0.214127 ns. (My earlier plan quoted 0.2296 ns from an ad-hoc snippet that had a sign error in the right-side interpolation; the value in the files is the correct one, verified by hand against the crossing samples.)
- The echoed input_v/time_s columns match the input file exactly as parsed by pandas; 116 of 4096 values differ from a Python-float() parse of the raw text by 1 ulp (relative 1e-16) — this is a pandas C-tokenizer rounding artifact on the generator's 17-significant-digit decimals, not a pipeline issue, and is far below any comparison tolerance.
